title: Zoom client secret in a token request Basic envelope or client_secret field
summary: The encoded Basic credential of a synthetic client id and client secret in the Authorization header of an OAuth or Server-to-Server token request, shown as a raw request, a quoted curl -H argument and a JSON header map, and a synthetic client_secret form field beside client_id.
rationale: Zoom documents the Basic Authorization header of token requests as the client ID and client secret joined by a colon and Base64 encoded, both for OAuth apps and for Server-to-Server OAuth apps, and its app credentials page also shows a client_secret form field in a development-credentials example. In a Basic envelope the secret exists only inside the encoded credential, so the extent is the whole encoded token, not a decoded secret-only span; the client id shares the envelope and is public. No prefix, alphabet or width of the secret is stated and none is claimed. The two Zoom client secret families are covered together because both pages document the same envelope; the pages do not say they are one credential or two.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the encoded credential after the Basic scheme in a token request, and the value of an exact client_secret form field, is treated as a credential; the Basic token is covered whole. Zoom documents the Basic envelope of client ID and client secret at the token endpoint and a client_secret form field in a development example (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and generic attribution are the project's decisions. That the envelope is Base64 of client id and secret joined by a colon is what the cited pages state; the envelope extent is a project decision. No prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: The Basic Authorization header is your Client ID and Client Secret by a colon (:) and Base64 encoded. Use PKCE to enable user authorization with a public client ID an no client secret, without the need for a backend server.
sources.locator: Request an access token, App Type: General, Exchange authorization code for access token

sources.supports: Encode the client ID and client secret in base64 format (with a colon between them, e.g. client_id:client_secret). Set up your API request header and include your encoded client ID and client secret using the 'Basic' HTTP Authentication Scheme
sources.locator: Generate access token, To generate an access token, steps 1 and 2

sources.supports: When setting up OAuth for user authorization, the development client ID and client secret are used to generate access tokens. (example POST https://zoom.us/oauth/token, x-www-form-urlencoded, with grant_type, code, redirect_uri, client_id and client_secret fields)
